subject.title: Keep Windows Companion aligned with current OpenClaw stable and beta releases

question: Should the Companion continue using a manually promoted, proof-backed LKG, or automatically follow OpenClaw’s latest stable tag while separately monitoring beta compatibility?
rationale: The repository already detects release drift, but choosing automatic latest-tag adoption versus a validated LKG changes the supported installer’s reliability contract, especially while the proposed stable has a known upstream startup regression.

options.title: Promote a validated LKG
options.body: Keep automated drift PRs, but merge a new stable pin only after exact tests and real Companion fresh-install and upgrade proof; run beta validation as a separate readiness lane.

options.title: Automatically follow stable
options.body: Make setup resolve the current stable tag automatically, accepting that upstream regressions can immediately affect new Windows installations.

options.title: Keep ad hoc manual pins
options.body: Continue updating the version only when someone notices drift, without a defined beta-readiness or promotion process.

recommendation.title: Promote a validated LKG
recommendation.body: Keep automated drift PRs, but merge a new stable pin only after exact tests and real Companion fresh-install and upgrade proof; run beta validation as a separate readiness lane.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent setup and release-path work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for deciding the supported-install promotion policy.
